name: cortados-routed-subagents
description: Routes every subagent spawned from this session through the CortadOS provider: S1 picks the cheapest capable model, it runs headless on the provider host, and its tool calls are bridged back to run on this machine. The main session stays on direct Claude.

providerUrl.title: Provider URL
providerUrl.description: CortadOS provider base URL that subagents route through (e.g. the Air on the tailnet).

providerTokenFile.title: Provider token file
providerTokenFile.description: Path to a file holding CORTADOS_PROVIDER_TOKEN. Read fresh at spawn time so the token is never stored in settings. A leading ~ is expanded to $HOME.

providerToken.title: Provider token (inline override)
providerToken.description: Optional inline token. When set it overrides providerTokenFile. Prefer the file so the token is not kept in settings.

model.title: Routed model id
model.description: The model id sent to the provider. 'cortados' lets S1 route; a concrete id pins one lane.

permissionMode.title: Permission mode for routed subagents
permissionMode.description: Headless permission mode. 'bypassPermissions' lets a routed subagent run Bash/edits unattended (full agentic, highest blast radius). 'acceptEdits' auto-approves file edits but blocks unattended Bash. 'default' blocks anything that needs a prompt.

allowedTools.title: Allowed tools (comma-separated)
allowedTools.description: Built-in tools a routed subagent has on this machine, passed as both --tools (availability, the real boundary) and --allowedTools (permission). Tools execute locally (bridged back from the routed model), so this is the real blast-radius control. Built-in tools only; MCP tools are controlled separately.

claudeBin.title: Claude binary
claudeBin.description: The claude executable used to run each routed subagent. Must be on PATH or an absolute path.

routeBackground.title: Route background subagents too
routeBackground.description: Off by default: background (run_in_background) subagents pass through to native handling, because a routed subagent runs under a 10-minute ceiling. Turn on only for short background tasks.

orchestratorMode.title: Orchestrator mode (brain only plans and delegates)
orchestratorMode.description: When on, a standing directive tells the main session to plan and delegate work to routed subagents. It is guidance, not a cage: the brain keeps its tools and may act directly when delegating is clearly wasteful, and it does browser/MCP steps itself (routed subagents have only built-in tools). Turn on orchestratorEnforce for a hard tool block. Subagents are unaffected.

orchestratorEnforce.title: Orchestrator enforce (hard-block non-allowlisted tools)
orchestratorEnforce.description: Off by default. When on together with orchestratorMode, every main-loop tool outside orchestratorAllowedTools is refused, so the brain cannot act even if it tried. Leave off unless you want a strict plan-only brain; it also blocks browser and connector tools the brain may need.

orchestratorAllowedTools.title: Tools the brain MAY use itself on the main loop
orchestratorAllowedTools.description: Used only when orchestratorEnforce is on: comma/space-separated allowlist of tools the main loop may run itself. Everything else (edits, shell, web, MCP tools, future tools) is refused and must be delegated. Agent and route_task are always allowed, and the desktop app's turn plumbing (update_plan, wrap_up, mark_chapter) is never blocked. An empty/invalid value falls back to the default.

subagentTimeoutMs.title: Routed subagent timeout (ms)
subagentTimeoutMs.description: How long a routed subagent may run before it is aborted. Max 600000 (10 min), Claude Code's own limit for a mod's process; larger values are clamped, fractions are rounded down, invalid values use the default.
